   - Backface culling: after transforming vertices to world/view space, compute each face's normal via cross product of two edges and cull faces whose normal points away from the camera (dot(normal, viewDir) <= 0).
2. Split each remaining quad face into 2 triangles (v0,v1,v2) and (v0,v2,v3).
3. Per-vertex Lambert lighting: for each triangle vertex compute the world-space normal (from the face normal, or averaged from adjacent faces for smoother shading — recommend computing per-vertex normals by averaging the normals of adjacent faces, then re-normalize, so Gouraud interpolation is visibly smooth), then diffuse = max(0, dot(normal, lightDir)) with a small ambient term. 9. Also add a short on-screen help line listing controls (W = wireframe, P = pause) and a title.
